title: Quiet deployment window protocol and rollback playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for a low-noise ("quiet window") release protocol to minimize customer-visible disruption during model or runtime deploys. Intended for small, sensitive rollouts where we want ultra-conservative traffic shaping and clear, rehearsed rollback steps.

Context / why this exists:
- Recent spike in regression rollbacks during busy hours. We need a repeatable plan that reduces signal noise and avoids broad customer impact.
- Approach: release during a low-traffic window, warm up a tiny cohort, run short golden-path checks, then slowly enlarge with strict automated thresholds.

Assumptions:
- We have routing control able to steer by client-id or region with 0.1% granularity.
- Observability hooks (latency, error rates, token-cost) emit within 30s buckets to the release dashboard.
- Feature flagging is available for immediate cutover.

Goals:
- No customer-facing errors >0.01% during rollout.
- Detect regressions within first 10m after initial warmup.
- Fully degradable to previous image within 2 minutes.

Quiet window scheduling (preferred):
1) Pick an 8-12 minute window in region local low-traffic (example: UTC 03:40 - 03:52).
2) Announce in #releases and the SRE oncall 30m prior.
3) Block any unrelated infra changes during the window.

Traffic plan (granular):
- t0: deploy model variant to canary pool (0% traffic). Run local smoke.
- t+2m: route 0.05% (by client hash) for 3 minutes.
- t+5m: if metrics green, move to 0.5% for 4 minutes.
- t+9m: if still green, move to 2% for 10 minutes, then 5% steady-state for a health check period (1h) before broader rollout.

Health checks and thresholds (automated):
- Latency p95 increase <= +20% absolute and <= +150ms.
- Error rate (5xx + client-visible generation errors) <= 0.01% absolute increase vs baseline.
- Token cost variance: alert if per-session token usage deviates > 30% (indicates prompt drift).
- Quality sentinel: run 60 synthetic prompts (golden set) on each cohort; fail if >3 prompts change pass/fail status.

Quick rollback triggers (auto):
- Any threshold breach above causes immediate automatic rollback to previous variant and an incident note.
- Manual rollback: oncall or release owner may execute with little friction (see commands).

Rollback commands (examples):
- Feature-flag cut: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN" "https://flags.redwood.ai/api/toggle" -d '{"flag":"use-new-variant","state":"off"}'
- Router reassign (kafka-route): kubectl exec -n routing router-ctrl -- /bin/sh -c "route set variant stable --clients all"
- If router unavailable: update load-balancer weight to 0 for canary pool via infra console.

Warmup checklist (pre-traffic):
- [ ] PR merged + image built and smoke-tested in staging. Link: GitHub PR above.
- [ ] Canary pool nodes are on same kernel / driver patch level.
- [ ] Warmup cache priming: run 200 short inference calls (1-2 tokens) to populate KV caches.
- [ ] Backup previous model snapshot and config (s3://release-backups/REL-8421/).
- [ ] Post-deploy synthetic runner ready and green.

Monitoring dashboard quick-view (what I watch):
- p50/p95/p99 latency graphs (all regions stacked).
- 5xx count and 4xx spikes.
- Token-per-session median and 99th percentile.
- Synthetic pass rate over rolling 10m.
- Cost burn estimate per minute for canary cohort (unexpected surge detector).

Post-rollout steps (if graduated):
- Annotate the deployment: PR, image SHA, release window, cohorts impacted.
- Run expanded golden set (~600 prompts) over 24h to detect slow regressions.
- Schedule 48h follow-up sync with SRE and product.

Open questions / TODOs (personal):
- Can we get router steering down to 0.01% for very sensitive tenants? (ask infra-rt)
- Should synthetic prompt runner include adversarial-styled prompts that previously caused regressions?
- Need a small CLI helper to atomically change traffic percents and run health checks — draft sketch TODO.

Notes about edge cases:
- If client pins exist (customer-specified model version), ensure cohort steering excludes pinned clients to avoid unexpected pin collisions.
- For private deployments, the quiet-window might be daytime — coordinate with customer ops.

Handy hacks / one-liners I use:
- quick health check: for i in {1..60}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SYN_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'; sleep 1; done | jq -r '.status' | sort | uniq -c
- force rollback (local): ./release-tools rollback --release REL-8421 --immediate

After-action template (fill after every window):
- who: (release owner)
- what: image sha / config changes
- when: window start/end
- what went well: 
- what failed / anomalies:
- follow-ups: assign owners and due dates

Scratchpad thoughts (brain dump):
- Could add a micro-quarantine group: if any 10m window shows a small regression, isolate those clients automatically and throttle them to reduced token budget while still running background tests. Might reduce blast radius.
- Might be worth pairing this with a short lived feature flag that reroutes only internal-monitoring clients first (canary-of-canary).

Last tested notes: 2025-02-14 — practiced once with model-x-stable->model-x-v2, observed a p95 spike at t+6m that auto-rolled back. Root cause: unexpected prompt expansion due to template change. Add template-change dimension to synthetic runner.

-- end of scratchpad --
